passages.text: MUMPS, called by Dr Cullen cynanche parotidaea, a swelling of the glands under the ears and about the angle of the jaw, which often extends to the neck, and makes the motion of the jaw painful.
It is contagious, attacks chiefly children and young persons, and often goes through a whole school or village as an epidemic.
As the swelling of the neck goes down, it often happens that the testicles in males, or the breasts in females, swell in its place; and this translation of the disease was called a metastasis.
The disease is seldom dangerous, and commonly goes off in a few days with a gentle sweat.
The cause is supposed to be a peculiar acrimony of the lymph, which settles in the glands.
The cure requires only that the patient keep warm and avoid cold, with a gentle purge; and if the swelling should leave the neck suddenly, it is to be recalled by warm applications to the part.
Mumps is a highly contagious viral disease caused by the mumps virus. The most typical sign is painful swelling of the parotid glands, the salivary glands in front of and below the ears.
Early symptoms include fever, headache and tiredness. Swelling of one or both parotid glands usually follows.
The virus spreads through respiratory droplets and saliva. Before vaccination, mumps was a common childhood disease worldwide.
Complications include inflammation of the testicles (orchitis), of the ovaries, of the breasts and of the pancreas, as well as meningitis and deafness.
Most people recover fully. Death from mumps is rare.
There is no specific treatment. Care aims at relieving the symptoms, for example with pain medicine.
Mumps can be prevented with a vaccine, usually given as part of the MMR vaccine together with measles and rubella. Vaccination has made the disease much less common.
After it multiplies in the throat and nearby lymph nodes, the virus spreads through the blood to other glands and organs, such as the testicles, ovaries, pancreas and brain.

reasons: Same headword in both: MUMPS and Mumps.
Rare terms appear in both: glands under the ears, testicles, breasts, contagious in children.
Parotitis scores well but covers every swelling of the parotid gland, not only mumps.

alignments.label: Glands below the ears

britannica.quote: a swelling of the glands under the ears

wikipedia.quote: painful swelling of the parotid glands

alignments.note: Same sign. Wikipedia names the glands: the parotid glands.

alignments.label: Contagious
alignments.note: Same fact, almost the same words.

alignments.label: Chiefly children

britannica.quote: attacks chiefly children and young persons

wikipedia.quote: mumps was a common childhood disease worldwide

alignments.note: Same fact in new words. Wikipedia adds that this was before vaccination.

alignments.label: Testicles and breasts

britannica.quote: the testicles in males, or the breasts in females, swell

wikipedia.quote: inflammation of the testicles (orchitis), of the ovaries, of the breasts

alignments.note: The 1817 observation holds. Wikipedia lists the same organs and more.

alignments.label: Metastasis

britannica.quote: this translation of the disease was called a metastasis

wikipedia.quote: the virus spreads through the blood to other glands and organs

alignments.note: Right observation, wrong mechanism. The disease does not move from the neck to the testicles. The virus reaches both through the blood. Today metastasis means the spread of a cancer.

alignments.label: Seldom dangerous

wikipedia.quote: as well as meningitis and deafness

alignments.note: Death is still rare, but Wikipedia lists serious complications such as meningitis and deafness that the 1817 entry does not mention.

alignments.label: Acrimony of the lymph

britannica.quote: a peculiar acrimony of the lymph

alignments.note: A change in knowledge. A virus causes the disease, not a fault of the lymph.

alignments.label: Keep warm

britannica.quote: keep warm and avoid cold, with a gentle purge

alignments.note: Care for comfort is still the only treatment. The purge and the warm applications to recall the swelling have no basis today.

alignments.label: MMR vaccine

wikipedia.quote: usually given as part of the MMR vaccine

alignments.note: The 1817 entry has no prevention. The vaccine made the disease much less common.

suggestedQuestions: Why did the 1817 entry call the swelling of the testicles a metastasis?
Is mumps as harmless as the 1817 entry says?

Why did the 1817 entry call the swelling.answer: The entry saw the swelling of the neck go down as the testicles or breasts swelled, and thought the disease moved from one place to the other [B3]. Wikipedia confirms that the testicles, ovaries and breasts can be affected [W4], but explains that the virus spreads through the blood to these organs [W8]. The observation holds; the idea that the disease moves does not.

Is mumps as harmless as the 1817 entry s.answer: Mostly. The entry calls it seldom dangerous [B4], and Wikipedia says most people recover fully and death is rare [W5]. But Wikipedia also lists meningitis and deafness among the complications [W4], and a vaccine now prevents the disease [W7].
